_note: Map v4's road surface model and everything made from it (MAP_README.md; map/model/). Every width, spacing, threshold and tolerance the v4 bake uses. Bump version after changing anything: the next bake redoes every tile and the game's tile cache drops the old ones. Map v3's own settings stay in data/map/bake.json (still read for terrain colours, surfaces, barriers, trees' density, buildings).

graph._note: densify: m between points added on gentle curves (OSM's own nodes never move); straightSpacing: m between points along straight pieces (for the height profile); maxTurnPerPoint: degrees a curve may turn between two points before more are added; corner: a turn sharper than this (degrees) stays a corner; jointMaxTurn: two roads meeting end to end turning more than this (degrees) get a junction patch instead of a shared cross-section; jointMaxWidthChange: m of width change a shared cross-section takes (more: a patch); borderNodes: a graph node where a road crosses a tile border

widths._note: Each road's width (m): the OSM width tag when there is one (the carriageway, kerb to kerb), else lanes × laneWidth + both shoulders, else the class's lanes (twoWay / oneWay: per direction on a one-way carriageway). visual = drivable + 2 × kerb (the kerb band is drawn, flush). multiplier: everything (1.0 is real size with these generous defaults). minDrivable: never narrower. Lanes and widths not tagged in OSM are marked estimated.
widths._sideBySide: Roads side by side that don't meet there (two carriageways of one road, a service road beside a street): the sides facing each other are narrowed so a gap of at least medianMin m stays between them (the real median kept, not filled), never below minHalf m from the centre line; eased along the road over easeLength m. Marked adjusted.

heights._note: The road surface's heights, solved on the graph: each way's elevation profile (spikes out: a running median over `median` points either side; then a Gaussian, `smooth` m) → junction heights and planes (the profiles' heights where they reach the junction, a least-squares plane through them no steeper than junctionMaxSlope) → each segment bent to meet its ends, then held to maxGrade and to maxGradeChange (change of grade per metre: no crest that throws a car) by relaxation. armEase: m over which a road eases from its own profile and camber onto a junction's plane. Bridges ease straight between their ends and are lifted overpassClearance over what they cross; tunnels likewise below.

junctions._note: Junction patches: each arm trimmed back to where its edges meet its neighbours' (plus kerbRadius, the corner's round), at least minTrim m, at most maxTrim m and never into the next junction (then the two become one cluster with one patch). A corner where the edges meet ahead is a curve round kerbRadius; one where they don't (a straight run past, the wide side of a fork) follows the edges round. minRibbon: the least road left between two junctions' trims before they merge. mergeDistance: junction nodes this close always share a patch. Holes in a patch smaller than minHoleArea m² or thinner than minHoleWidth m (on average) are slivers, filled; bigger ones are islands and medians, kept. closeGap: cracks in a patch's outline narrower than this (m) are closed (0: off — Clipper's offsets leave artefacts on dense curves).

surface._note: The surface's cross-section: visual edge, kerb's inner edge (drivable edge), half way, crown — mirrored. skirtDepth: a strip down from the visual edge (drawn only, not solid) so the ground's sink never shows as a gap. Dead ends run capLength m past their last node. Markings (cheap: one vertex-coloured mesh) by region style; lines markingWidth m wide, raised markingLift m, dashed dash/gap m.

terrain._note: The ground under and round the road surface, in the height grid itself (so the drawn ground and the physics' heightfield match): every grid point under the surface or within margin m of it set sink m under the nearest road surface (margin is at least the grid cell's diagonal: no terrain triangle can reach up into the road); then sloping back to the natural ground (1 : slope, minBlend to maxBlend m). The terrain's simplified meshes are drawn lowered by their own error, so they can't come up through a road at a distance. Bridges: the ground kept bridgeClearance under the deck (underBridge away from its ends). Tunnels: the ground over them kept as a roof.

collision._note: Road collision: each tile's road triangles plus apron m of its neighbours' past its edge (overlapping copies of the same surface: no edge at the border for a wheel or the car's body to catch), as one trimesh with Rapier's internal-edge fix. Building colliders never on a road: a hull over the road surface (any point of it within roadClearance m) is trimmed back off it, or dropped if too little is left (logged). Bumps: the most vertical acceleration (m/s², the car's body, beyond gravity) allowed crossing junctions, bridge ends and tile borders.

exclusion._note: The exclusion mask (baked, inspectable): a 1 m raster of where nothing may stand — every road surface on every layer plus buffer m, junctions, car parks, tunnel portals (portal m round each end), railways (railway m each side), and the ground under every bridge deck plus deckMargin m. A tree is placed only if no masked cell is under its crown (crownRadius × its scale); under a deck only if allowUnderDecks and its crown's top is clearance m under the deck (the clearance stored in the data). Lamps and signs: their foot.

lamps._note: Street lamps: OSM's (highway=street_lamp, man_made=street_lamp) first; then estimated ones from the road model on lit roads (lit=yes, or urban classes when lit isn't tagged; never lit=no): spacing m by kind, at the kerb (offset m outside the visual edge) or in a median wider than medianMin m, both sides of roads at least bothSidesWidth m wide; one at every junction corner of a lit road, two at crossings; tunnels continuous at tunnel m, on the wall. Never in a lane, on a road surface, or under a deck (the exclusion mask). A mapped lamp within mappedRadius m stands in for an estimated one. Height, arm, colour, and the rendering's real-light count.

barriers._note: Railings from the model: OSM's barrier lines (never on a road surface: each piece tested along its whole length against the exclusion mask), and estimated ones (flagged) both sides of bridges, motorway edges, medians at least median m wide, and road edges with the ground dropping more than drop m within reach m for at least minRun m (none within skipNearJunction m of a junction patch). Chained with no gaps.

bake._note: workers: tiles written in parallel (0: one per core less one); gzip level (9 is 3% smaller and twice as slow as 6)
